order: The rules apply in the order this list gives them, first to last, each one to every occurrence, one text block at a time — the order the reading view applies them in and the order their hits are counted in. Order decides: a rule whose find an earlier rule has already replaced fires zero times, and the build FAILS on a rule that fires zero times, so a redundant rule is caught rather than shipped. The classes are grouped in the order the pipeline needs them: opener (the divisions, which the extraction needs before it can find a section), digit (printed numbers and note markers, each pinned to its line), reading (the print's own word, where this edition records it), review (a passage whose harm is real but whose reading is not determinable — recorded as left, never deleted).

classes.opener: a division number the transcription mangled, where the print has a reading
classes.digit: a printed number or a note marker read through an OCR digit confusion
classes.reading: the print's word for a damaged run, recorded from this edition's own context or from the parallel edition — the reading view shows it; the transcription is never edited
classes.review: a passage whose harm is real but whose correct reading cannot be determined from the source: recorded with action "leave", so its damage stays visible

edits.replace: and affords a friendly branch to the suppliant
edits.note: SUPERSEDES the recorded LEAVE. The run stands between the anchors "crowns-" and "petitioner", and the 1823 parallel reads "and affords a friendly branch to the suppliant petitioner" — so the replacement carries the WHOLE slot between the anchors. A half repair (the earlier pass proposed only "and affords a friendly") would be worse than the leave: it yields a sentence that reads as the author's error.

the PAGE FURNITURE of a page break, not words. It stands alone in its own block between section 6's close ("the vestment of the celestial Gods. 1") and section 7's opener ("7. Why, therefore..."), and the 1823 parallel runs straight from "celestial Gods." to "7. Why" with nothing between — so whatever the print has here is its page number and running head, and the OCR destroyed both beyond reading. Left visible rather than guessed: a reading invented for a page number would be a reading the edition does not have.
